To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the pattern of token exchanges under a second-order FR schedule with a fixed ratio FR exchange schedule is similar to the pattern of lever presses under a simple FR schedule; and 2) the pattern of exchanges under the same second-order FR schedule but with a VR exchange schedule is similar in many respects to the pattern of exchanges and lever presses under a second-order VR schedule.

the patterns of behavior that characterize simple fixed-ratio schedules of token reinforcement are also characteristic of behavior that is reinforced by a second-order schedule that includes a fixed-ratio exchange period.
the effects of the ratio schedule in a second-order schedule are similar to those of the ratio schedule when the second-order schedule is not present.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis and modification of behavior maintained by second-order schedules of token exchange.
the effects of altering the schedule of reinforcement on the temporal patterning of behavior.
the development of a new model of second-order schedules of token-reinforcement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present data are consistent with the view that the exchange period schedule is a determinant of response rate.

the present results support the notion that the exchange period schedule functions to control the temporal distribution of reinforcement, and thus the temporal distribution of behavior, in the same way as a simple fixed-ratio or variable-ratio schedule of food reinforcement.
the second-order schedule, as defined here, is an appropriate model for the analysis of complex schedules of reinforcement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of the exchange period schedule were to increase response rates and decrease response pauses.
second-order schedules of token exchange can produce performance patterns that are similar to those obtained under simple schedules of reinforcement.
second-order schedules of token exchange are not simply additive, but that they interact with the component schedules in complex ways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same behavioral phenomena can be produced in rats by second-order schedules of reinforcement that have no direct correspondence to the first-order schedules that produce them.
the effects of the second-order schedule are not limited to the component token schedules, and that the effects of exchange period schedule manipulations are not limited to exchange periods.
the same principles that have been used to explain simple ratio schedules of reinforcement can be extended to second-order schedules.
